# Results — Study 430 (Klinger Volume Oscillator)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **Klinger's
long-term volume oscillator leads price, so timing the index with it beats buy-and-hold** —
tested as a daily long/flat (and long/short) timing rule on SPY. The oscillator is computed on
closes/volumes up to *t*; the position is held over *t+1* (one execution lag). All returns are
**excess of cash** (excess-vs-excess Sharpe race) and **net** of one-way costs × NAV turnover.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **OHLCV**, auto-adjusted (total-return proxy) — SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (the partial current month is dropped) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; **5,385** sessions) |
| Fingerprint (SPY close) | `63d0db58b0a8` |
| Indicator | Klinger Volume Oscillator **KVO(34, 55, 13)** (Klinger's standard spans) |
| Rule / lag / costs | headline = **KVO > 0 long/flat**; signal at close *t*, position over *t+1* (one shift); **1 bp** one-way × NAV turnover; 50 bps/yr borrow on any short leg |
| Robustness panel | SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, EEM, GLD (same window) |

## The headline race — Klinger long/flat vs buy-and-hold (net, excess-of-cash)

| Rule | net Sharpe | CAGR | max drawdown | time-in-mkt | turnover/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold | **+0.645** | +11.0% | −55.2% | 100% | — |
| **Klinger KVO>0 long/flat** | **+0.382** | +3.7% | −48.9% | 53% | 21.9 |
| 200-day SMA filter | **+0.776** | +8.5% | −20.9% | 77% | 5.8 |
| MACD(12,26,9) | +0.548 | — | — | — | — |

The "leading" indicator **trails everything**. Klinger's net Sharpe (**+0.38**) is below
buy-and-hold (**+0.65**), below MACD (**+0.55**), and far below the dumbest competitor — a
one-line **200-day moving average** (**+0.78**), which also has a *much* smaller drawdown and a
quarter of the turnover. The only place Klinger looks defensible is drawdown (−49% vs −55%), but
it pays for that with so much forgone upside that the risk-adjusted return still loses.

## The decisive test — HAC *t* of the daily difference

The Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the per-day (Klinger − benchmark) excess-return difference vs 0
(autocorrelation-robust, because daily strategy returns are serially dependent):

| Difference | HAC *t* | Reading |
|---|--:|---|
| Klinger − buy-and-hold | **−2.87** | reliably **worse** than holding |
| Klinger − 200d SMA | −1.78 | worse (not quite significant) |
| Klinger − MACD | −0.94 | worse (insignificant) |

The desk's bar for a **positive** Signal is HAC *t* ≥ +2. Klinger is nowhere near it — if
anything it clears the bar on the **wrong side** (*t* = −2.87 vs buy-and-hold).

## The luck test — a coin beats Klinger's timing

Klinger is long ~53% of days. Block-shuffling the held-position series into **3,000** random
schedules (21-day blocks preserve persistence and time-in-market) and re-booking each net of the
same costs:

| | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|
| Klinger actual timing | +0.382 |
| Random-schedule **median** | **+0.444** |
| **p(random schedule ≥ Klinger)** | **0.669** |

A random schedule with the same exposure beats Klinger's actual timing **67%** of the time, and
the *typical* coin does **better**. Knowing *when* the oscillator is positive carries no
information about the next day's return.

## Rule variants — nothing rescues it

| Variant | net Sharpe | HAC *t* vs buy-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| KVO > 0, long/flat | +0.382 | −2.87 |
| KVO > 0, long/short | **−0.203** | −2.92 |
| KVO > signal, long/flat | +0.138 | −4.09 |
| KVO > signal, long/short | **−0.481** | −4.14 |

The signal-line crossing is *worse* than the zero-cross, and **both long/short legs go
negative** — shorting on a negative KVO is actively harmful.

## Cost sweep — behind even at zero cost

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* vs buy-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.402 | −2.80 |
| 1.0 bps | +0.382 | −2.87 |
| 2.0 bps | +0.363 | −2.95 |
| 5.0 bps | +0.304 | −3.18 |

Even at **zero cost** Klinger lands at ~0.40, below buy-and-hold's 0.65. The killer is the
signal, not the friction; costs are salt in the wound.

## Panel — it loses everywhere

| Ticker | Klinger Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | HAC *t* vs hold |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | +0.382 | +0.645 | −2.87 |
| QQQ | +0.652 | +0.778 | −2.65 |
| IWM | +0.393 | +0.470 | −1.43 |
| DIA | +0.394 | +0.617 | −2.48 |
| EEM | +0.203 | +0.400 | −2.07 |
| GLD | +0.317 | +0.677 | −2.96 |

Klinger is **below** buy-and-hold on every one of six ETFs. A real leading signal would win
*somewhere*; losing everywhere is what a non-signal looks like.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where volume **genuinely leads price** by a day (knob `edge`):

| planted edge | Klinger Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | HAC *t* vs hold | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0** (no info) | −0.633 | −0.355 | **−0.51** | 0.981 |
| **3.0** (volume leads) | +5.613 | +0.439 | **+8.21** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted lead the rule does not beat buy-and-hold (*t* ≈ 0, placebo *p* = 0.98 — no
false positive); with a **strong** planted lead it lights up massively (*t* = +8.21, placebo
*p* = 0.000). The harness *can* detect volume-leads-price when it is really there — so the dead
real-tape result is a **true negative**, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Klinger long/flat net Sharpe **+0.38** vs buy-and-hold **+0.65**; HAC *t*
  of the daily difference = **−2.87** (reliably *worse*). No variant clears buy-and-hold; the
  long/short legs go negative. Nowhere near the desk's *t ≥ 2* bar for a positive edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Loses the race at every cost level (~22 round-trips/yr) and is beaten
  by a one-line 200d SMA (+0.78). There is no residual edge to deploy.
- **"Volume leads price"? — BUSTED.** A block-shuffled random schedule with the same
  time-in-market beats Klinger's timing **p = 0.67** of the time. The oscillator is a lagging
  difference-of-EMAs of a volume series; a low-pass filter delays, it does not anticipate.
